note: Use with elders and anyone you don't know well.
Kaisi when it's about a woman, kaisa for one man or thing.
Also used for one person, to show respect.
Acchi for feminine words, acche for plural or respect.
At the start of a sentence it can also just mark a question.
Kya haal hai = how are things.
Many Hindi feelings work as 'to me': mujhe pata = to me it's known.
Thodi Hindi, thodi chai: both feminine.
Mujhe Hindi aati hai = Hindi comes to me, i.e. I know Hindi.
Samajh nahin aaya = it didn't come into understanding.
Samajh gayi = understood, said by or to a woman.
Also shows something has happened: pet bhar gaya = my stomach got full.
Added after a name or title to show respect.
With hain it politely introduces someone.
Used fondly for any younger person.
Its meaning depends on the phrase.
Kaisa laga = how did it feel, i.e. did you like it.
In wishes like mubaarak ho, it means 'may it be'.
The form used before a past action.
Of with feminine words (Diwali ki); did with mehnat.
Jeete raho = may you live long.
